official_measurement_examples.name: SPZ screening role
official_measurement_examples.fact: Environment Agency's March 2026 merged SPZ dataset describes source protection zones as an initial screening tool for groundwater-resource impacts, not a complete planning or permitting decision.

official_measurement_examples.name: SPZ1 definition
official_measurement_examples.fact: Environment Agency guidance defines SPZ1 using the larger of the statutory 50 metre area or groundwater travel time of up to 50 days to a potable abstraction point.

official_measurement_examples.name: SPZ2 definition
official_measurement_examples.fact: SPZ2 can be based on distance thresholds linked to abstraction volume or groundwater travel time up to 400 days, with the largest applicable area used.

official_measurement_examples.name: Safeguard zone distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: The April 2026 Drinking Water Groundwater Safeguard Zones dataset identifies areas where additional pollution-control measures are needed and notes that safeguard-zone geometry may not coincide exactly with SPZ geometry.

official_measurement_examples.name: Groundwater vulnerability update
official_measurement_examples.fact: The groundwater vulnerability dataset updated 16 July 2026 shows susceptibility to pollutants discharged at ground level and supersedes the previous 100k Environment Agency vulnerability data.

official_measurement_examples.name: Permit separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Environment Agency guidance updated 20 April 2026 states groundwater or water-discharge activities may require environmental permits; a permit is separate from planning permission.

official_measurement_examples.name: Exclusion limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Groundwater activity exclusions apply only to specified very low-risk cases and the Environment Agency can determine whether an activity meets exclusion conditions; an exclusion must not be assumed from map location alone.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning Data maturity
official_measurement_examples.fact: Planning Data's drinking-water safeguard-zone consideration records that the planning need is not yet fully defined, so its design-stage status must not be treated as a complete statutory planning rule.

core_rules: SPZ geometry is groundwater-risk screening evidence not planning permission
SPZ1 must preserve its current statutory distance or travel-time definition
SPZ2 must preserve abstraction-volume and travel-time logic
SPZ3 is total catchment evidence and not an exclusion zone
SPZ4 special-interest areas must not be assumed to exist everywhere
safeguard zones are not identical to source protection zones
groundwater vulnerability mapping is not proof of actual contamination
an environmental permit is distinct from planning permission
planning permission is not a groundwater activity permit
permit exclusions must be matched to current conditions and cannot be assumed
septic or sewage general binding rules are distinct from development consent
groundwater guidance does not determine land ownership access or abstraction rights
historic SPZ geometry must retain revision date and modelling context
Planning Data design-stage considerations must retain maturity limitations
no parcel groundwater clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
